key_insight: A monolayer graphene front contact improves nitride-based AlInN/Si solar cell performance by boosting current collection and efficiency without materially changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene offers a low-temperature, semitransparent alternative to conventional contacts for integrating higher-performance nitride-based photovoltaics on silicon.
method: Prepared AlxIn1-xN solar cells on p-type Si(100) with an amorphous-Si buffer layer.
Studied three Al compositions: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43.
Transferred a monolayer graphene film onto the device front surface as a semitransparent conductive contact.
evidence_signal: Devices with graphene were evaluated under illuminated and dark conditions, and the abstract reports higher short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency for all compositions while Voc stayed largely unchanged.
watch_item: Performance gains are promising, but large-area transfer quality and contact consistency of graphene could affect reproducibility in practical fabrication.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
